meta.name: Microsoft Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate (DP-600)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 scenario-style questions across the four DP-600 domains: plan and manage an analytics solution, prepare and serve data, implement and manage semantic models, explore and analyze data. v1.1: +10 — lakehouse vs warehouse, shortcuts, deployment pipelines, Direct Lake fallback, Git integration, XMLA tools, saveAsTable, default vs custom models, cross-database T-SQL, Gen2 incremental refresh.

questions.question: An analytics engineer must build a Power BI semantic model in Microsoft Fabric that queries multi-billion-row Delta tables in a lakehouse with sub-second visual response times, without scheduling refreshes and without importing the data. Which storage mode delivers this?
options: Import mode against the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint with daily incremental refresh
DirectQuery against the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint with auto-aggregations enabled
Direct Lake mode against the lakehouse Delta tables in OneLake
Composite mode combining DirectQuery to the warehouse and Import for lookup tables
questions.explanation: Direct Lake mode reads Parquet pages from the Delta tables in OneLake directly into the VertiPaq engine on demand, with no data duplication and no scheduled refresh. Import would require a copy and refresh schedule; DirectQuery pushes each query to the SQL endpoint which adds latency on large tables; composite mode still imports a slice. Direct Lake is the unique Fabric mode that combines Import-like speed with DirectQuery-like freshness.

questions.question: A team manages curated tables in an Azure SQL Database that must be queried from a Fabric lakehouse with near real-time freshness, no ETL code, and a single read-only Delta copy maintained automatically in OneLake. Which Fabric feature meets all three requirements?
options: OneLake shortcut to the Azure SQL Database tables
A Dataflow Gen2 with incremental refresh into the lakehouse
A Data Pipeline copy activity that runs every five minutes
Mirroring of the Azure SQL Database into Fabric
questions.explanation: Fabric Mirroring continuously replicates an operational database (Azure SQL DB, Cosmos DB, Snowflake, etc.) into OneLake as read-only Delta tables with near real-time latency and no ETL to author. Shortcuts only work against file-based sources like ADLS Gen2 or another OneLake item, not against an Azure SQL DB. Pipelines and Dataflows are scheduled ETL with higher latency and code/maintenance overhead.

questions.question: An analytics engineer needs to enforce that sales managers only see rows for their assigned region in a Power BI report served from a Fabric semantic model. The same model is consumed by an Excel pivot and by a paginated report. Where should the row filter be implemented so it applies consistently across all clients?
options: As a visual-level filter on every page of the Power BI report
As a WHERE clause in the SQL view that the semantic model imports from
As a row-level security (RLS) role with a DAX FILTER expression on the dimension table, mapped to the manager's UPN via USERPRINCIPALNAME()
As a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label on the workspace that limits row export
questions.explanation: Row-level security defined on the semantic model is enforced by the Analysis Services engine at query time, so it applies to every client that queries the model — Power BI, Excel via Analyze in Excel, paginated reports, and the XMLA endpoint. Visual filters can be bypassed by editing the report; SQL views only protect Import-time queries but not DirectQuery/Direct Lake refreshes initiated by other users; sensitivity labels classify and govern content but do not filter rows.

questions.question: A workspace administrator wants developers to author semantic models and reports in Visual Studio Code and Power BI Desktop, branch the work in Azure DevOps, and have changes promoted from Dev to Test to Prod with environment-specific connection strings. Which combination should be configured?
options: Fabric REST APIs invoked from a single nightly Azure Function that overwrites Prod from Dev
Export each item as a .pbix file nightly and check it into the repo manually
A shared OneDrive folder for the .pbip projects and manual workspace-level overrides
Git integration on each workspace plus deployment pipelines with rules for connection-string parameters
questions.explanation: Fabric's Git integration syncs workspace items (semantic models, reports, notebooks, pipelines) as .pbip / source folders into an Azure DevOps or GitHub repo, giving developers branch-based authoring. Deployment pipelines then promote items Dev to Test to Prod with parameter and data-source rules to swap connection strings per environment. Manual .pbix exports, OneDrive sharing, or bespoke REST scripts lose lineage and lifecycle controls.

questions.question: A measure must return year-to-date Sales for the currently selected period in a report based on the date dimension marked as a date table. The model contains 'Sales'[Amount] and 'Date'[Date]. Which DAX expression is correct?
options: Sales YTD = SUMX('Sales', 'Sales'[Amount])
Sales YTD = TOTALYTD(SUM('Sales'[Amount]))
Sales YTD = CALCULATE(SUM('Sales'[Amount]), DATESYTD('Date'[Date]))
Sales YTD = CALCULATE(SUM('Sales'[Amount]), ALL('Date'))
questions.explanation: CALCULATE with the DATESYTD time-intelligence function modifies the date filter context to all dates from January 1 up to and including the last date in the current filter context, producing year-to-date totals. TOTALYTD requires a date column as its second argument, so the syntax shown is incomplete and will error. SUMX without CALCULATE ignores time context, and CALCULATE with ALL('Date') removes all date filters, returning the grand total — not YTD.

questions.question: A Dataflow Gen2 cleans and joins multiple CSV files in ADLS Gen2, then publishes to a lakehouse table. Downstream queries that consume merged intermediate steps re-evaluate the source files on every refresh and the run is much slower than expected. Which change addresses the redundant work?
options: Disable staging on all queries so they run end-to-end in the dataflow engine without intermediate writes
Enable staging on the intermediate merge queries so their outputs are materialized to the Fabric staging lakehouse and reused
Move the join logic into a downstream notebook and remove it from the dataflow
Convert the dataflow to a Data Pipeline copy activity with a tumbling window trigger
questions.explanation: When staging is enabled, Dataflow Gen2 materializes a query result to the hidden Fabric staging lakehouse / warehouse so downstream queries can read the staged data instead of re-evaluating the source. Disabling staging forces in-memory re-evaluation and makes the symptom worse. Moving logic to a notebook is a larger rewrite and not required. A Pipeline copy activity is a flat copy, not a Power Query transformation engine.

questions.question: An analytics engineer needs to query a Fabric semantic model from a Python notebook to validate measure results and pull table data into a pandas DataFrame for ad-hoc analysis, without exporting to CSV. Which Fabric capability should they use?
options: The Power BI REST API GetQueryResults endpoint with manual JSON parsing
Copy the .pbix file to OneLake and read it with PyArrow
An on-premises data gateway with an ODBC driver pointing at the model
Semantic Link (the sempy library) inside a Fabric notebook
questions.explanation: Semantic Link (sempy) is the Fabric Python library that lets notebooks list workspace models, evaluate DAX measures, and materialize semantic-model tables as pandas DataFrames over the XMLA endpoint. The REST API does not return tabular query results in a DataFrame-friendly way, an on-prem gateway is for on-prem sources, and .pbix files are not designed to be parsed as Parquet by PyArrow.

questions.question: A semantic model in Direct Lake mode is consumed by a high-concurrency Power BI report. During peak hours users see queries fall back to DirectQuery, slowing visuals. Which two factors most commonly trigger this fallback? (Choose the option that lists both correctly.)
options: Exceeding the SKU's column or row guardrails for Direct Lake, and the underlying Delta table being written to during the query
A measure using TIME-intelligence DAX functions, and the report using bookmarks
A composite model with an Import table, and the workspace being attached to a Pro license instead of a capacity
A user being assigned a row-level security role, and the model containing calculated columns
questions.explanation: Direct Lake falls back to DirectQuery on the lakehouse SQL endpoint when the model exceeds the capacity SKU guardrails (rows per table, columns per table, model size) or when the Delta table is being written to (framing in progress). Time-intelligence DAX, bookmarks, RLS, and calculated columns do not by themselves trigger fallback. A composite Import table is supported alongside Direct Lake without forcing fallback for the Direct Lake tables.

questions.question: A team must analyze high-volume IoT telemetry arriving from Event Hubs with sub-second query latency over the last 30 days and KQL ad-hoc exploration, while keeping older data accessible for periodic reporting. Which Fabric item is the right primary store for the hot data?
options: A lakehouse Delta table refreshed every minute by a Spark structured streaming job
A KQL Database in an Eventhouse, with OneLake availability turned on for the table
A Warehouse table populated by a Data Pipeline copy activity every minute
A Power BI Direct Lake semantic model with auto page refresh set to one second
questions.explanation: Eventhouse with a KQL Database is the Fabric Real-Time Intelligence engine designed for high-throughput time-series and log ingestion with sub-second KQL queries. Enabling OneLake availability also exposes the same data as Delta in OneLake so other engines can read it for reporting on older partitions. Minute-level Spark or Pipeline writes cannot match KQL latency, and a semantic model is a query layer, not a primary store.

questions.question: An analytics engineer needs to identify which DAX measure is causing a slow Power BI visual and inspect the storage-engine vs formula-engine time of each query. Which tool inside Power BI Desktop should they open first?
options: Performance Analyzer, then copy the query into DAX Studio to view server timings
Query Diagnostics in Power Query Editor
View Native Query on the source
The Refresh History pane in the Power BI service
questions.explanation: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop records each visual's DAX query and duration. The captured query can be copied into DAX Studio, where Server Timings break the duration into Storage Engine (SE) versus Formula Engine (FE) time and surface the actual queries sent to VertiPaq or DirectQuery. Query Diagnostics is for Power Query M, View Native Query inspects fold-down to the source, and Refresh History only shows dataset refresh runs.

questions.question: A semantic model defines 18 separate time-intelligence measures (MTD, QTD, YTD, PY, YoY%, etc.) for each of 12 base measures, resulting in over 200 measures and an unwieldy field list. Which feature consolidates the time-intelligence logic and presents users with a single 'Time Calculation' selector?
options: Calculation groups in the semantic model
A composite model with an aggregations table
Field parameters in the report
Implicit measures on the date dimension
questions.explanation: Calculation groups define a set of calculation items (MTD, QTD, YTD, PY, YoY%) that can be applied to any explicit measure at query time, replacing N base measures times M variants with a single dimension users select. Field parameters swap which field is plotted but do not transform a measure. Composite models with aggregations are a performance pattern, and implicit measures (auto-aggregations on columns) cannot encode time-intelligence patterns.

questions.question: Governance requires that sensitive financial reports built in Fabric inherit the 'Confidential\Finance' classification from the source warehouse and that the label persists when users export to Excel or PowerPoint. Which capability enforces this end-to-end?
options: Workspace-level access roles set to Contributor only
Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels with inheritance configured on the semantic model and downstream items
A capacity-level workload setting that disables export to Excel
Row-level security roles that map finance UPNs to a hidden filter table
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels can be applied to OneLake items, semantic models, and reports in Fabric. Inheritance propagates the source's label to downstream items and persists into exported Excel and PowerPoint files, where Azure Information Protection enforces the encryption and usage rights. Workspace roles control access, not classification; disabling export blocks a channel but does not classify content; RLS filters rows but does not label exports.

questions.question: In Microsoft Fabric, one team's engineers transform data with Spark notebooks while analysts insist on writing full T-SQL DML (INSERT/UPDATE) against curated tables. Which item types support each group's PRIMARY write workload?
options: Lakehouse for the Spark engineers; Warehouse for the T-SQL analysts
Warehouse for the Spark engineers; Lakehouse for the T-SQL analysts
KQL database for the engineers; semantic model for the analysts' DML
Both groups must share a Warehouse, since lakehouses store no tables
questions.explanation: The lakehouse is the Spark-first item — notebooks read/write Delta tables natively, and its SQL analytics endpoint is read-only T-SQL. The warehouse is the T-SQL-first item with full DML/DDL support. Both store Delta in OneLake, so each team can still read the other's data; KQL databases target real-time telemetry and semantic models aren't writable stores.

questions.question: Curated Delta tables already exist in an ADLS Gen2 account owned by another platform team. Fabric users need to query them from a lakehouse WITHOUT duplicating the data or building a copy pipeline. What should be created?
options: A Dataflow Gen2 with incremental refresh copying the tables into OneLake each hour
A OneLake shortcut in the lakehouse pointing at the ADLS Gen2 location
A Copy activity in a Data pipeline landing snapshots into the Files area nightly
A mirrored database configured against the storage account's blob endpoint
questions.explanation: Shortcuts virtualize external storage (ADLS Gen2, S3, GCS, other OneLake locations) into the lakehouse namespace — queries read the source directly, no duplication, no refresh schedule, instant consistency. Dataflows and Copy activities are copy machinery; mirroring replicates operational databases (SQL, Cosmos, Snowflake), not arbitrary storage accounts.

questions.question: Fabric content must flow Dev → Test → Prod with controlled promotion, environment-specific data source rules, and comparison of what differs between stages. Which Fabric capability provides this?
options: Deployment pipelines, assigning a workspace per stage and deploying with deployment rules
Exporting each item as a .pbip project file and importing it manually into the next workspace at every stage of the release
OneLake shortcuts from the production workspace into the development lakehouse
Workspace roles, granting developers Viewer in Prod and Admin in the Dev workspace
questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines bind Dev/Test/Prod workspaces into stages with one-click promotion, per-stage deployment rules (swap connections/parameters), and a diff view of changed items. Manual export/import has no rules or comparison; shortcuts share data, not content lifecycle; workspace roles control access, not promotion.

questions.question: A Direct Lake semantic model sometimes answers queries much slower than usual, and monitoring shows those queries were served via DirectQuery. What causes a Direct Lake model to fall back like this?
options: The Fabric capacity entered a paused or throttled state during those windows, forcing all semantic model traffic through import mode caches instead
Row-level security on the model always disables Direct Lake for every affected user
The model exceeded Direct Lake guardrails (or queried unsupported objects such as SQL views), so the engine fell back to DirectQuery through the SQL endpoint
A scheduled refresh was running concurrently, which locks Delta tables for reading
questions.explanation: Direct Lake reads Delta files directly, but falls back to DirectQuery when guardrails are exceeded (row counts/model size for the SKU) or when the model references things only the SQL endpoint can resolve — like views. Fallback is per-query and silent except for latency. Paused capacity fails outright; RLS works in Direct Lake (defined in the model); Delta reads aren't locked by refresh.

questions.question: An analytics team wants its Fabric workspace items version-controlled: commits on every change, branches for features, pull-request review before merge. What does Fabric provide natively?
options: Workspace Git integration, connecting the workspace to an Azure DevOps or GitHub repository
Automatic OneLake snapshots of every item taken on a fixed fifteen-minute schedule
OneLake shortcuts created from the production workspace back into the development lakehouse so item changes replicate automatically
Semantic model backup files written to ADLS Gen2 by the XMLA endpoint on commit
questions.explanation: Workspace-level Git integration syncs supported item definitions to a repo branch: changes commit from the workspace, branches and PRs follow normal Git flow, and workspaces can sync from a branch (the basis of branch-per-developer patterns). Snapshots, API polling and XMLA backups are not source control.

questions.question: A modeler wants to manage a Fabric semantic model with Tabular Editor and run DAX queries from DAX Studio. What must be true for these external tools to connect?
options: The XMLA endpoint is enabled for read-write on the capacity, and the tools connect via the workspace's XMLA connection string
The model must first be exported to a .pbix file and reopened in Power BI Desktop
External tools require the model to be migrated from Direct Lake to import mode first
An on-premises data gateway must be installed and registered to broker every external tool connection into the Fabric service
questions.explanation: Fabric capacities expose the XMLA endpoint; with read-write enabled in capacity settings, tools speaking the Analysis Services protocol (Tabular Editor, DAX Studio, SSMS) connect straight to the workspace and operate on deployed models. No .pbix export, storage-mode migration, or gateway is involved for cloud-to-cloud connections.

questions.question: In a Fabric notebook, transformed Spark DataFrame results must land in the lakehouse as a managed Delta table named gold_sales, replacing prior contents each run. Which statement does this?
options: df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("gold_sales")
df.toPandas().to_csv("/lakehouse/default/Tables/gold_sales.csv")
df.createOrReplaceTempView("gold_sales")
spark.sql("COPY INTO gold_sales FROM source_dataframe WITH (MODE = 'REPLACE', FORMAT = 'DELTA')")
questions.explanation: saveAsTable with the delta format and overwrite mode writes a managed Delta table into the lakehouse Tables area — discoverable by the SQL endpoint and semantic models. CSV in Files isn't a Delta table; a temp view exists only for the Spark session; the COPY syntax shown isn't valid Spark SQL.

questions.question: What is the recommended practice regarding the DEFAULT semantic model that Fabric creates for a lakehouse or warehouse, when a team needs governed measures, RLS and a curated star schema for reporting?
options: Add the measures and security roles directly to the default semantic model, since it stays synchronized with the underlying tables automatically
Create a separate custom semantic model over the curated tables and build measures, relationships and RLS there
Delete the default model so Fabric regenerates it with the curated design on next refresh
Export the default model weekly and re-import it as a backup of the reporting layer
questions.explanation: The default model is a convenience layer managed by the system; serious reporting should use a purpose-built custom semantic model where you control tables included, relationships, measures, RLS roles and lifecycle (Git, deployment pipelines). Building on the default couples you to system behavior; deleting it doesn't produce a curated design; exports aren't governance.

questions.question: An analyst on the warehouse needs to join a warehouse table to a table that lives in a lakehouse in the SAME workspace, entirely in T-SQL. What makes this possible?
options: Cross-database queries using three-part names against the lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint
It is impossible in T-SQL — lakehouse data must first be copied into warehouse tables with a pipeline before any join can run
Only via a Spark notebook that writes the join result back into the warehouse tables area
Defining an external table in the warehouse with OPENROWSET over the lakehouse files
questions.explanation: Within a workspace, the warehouse can query other warehouses and lakehouse SQL endpoints with three-part naming (lakehouse_name.schema.table) — joins across items run in one T-SQL statement, no copying. Spark and pipelines work but aren't required; OPENROWSET over files bypasses the Delta table abstraction unnecessarily.

questions.question: A Dataflow Gen2 ingests a large transactional table daily, but reprocessing all history every run is slow and wasteful. Only recent rows ever change. What should the engineer enable?
options: Incremental refresh on the dataflow, defining the date column and refresh window so only recent partitions reprocess
Staging disabled on every query so transformations stream without persistence
A second identical dataflow scheduled to run hourly so the reprocessing load is spread more evenly across the whole day
Fast copy mode, which automatically deduplicates previously loaded rows on ingest
questions.explanation: Incremental refresh in Dataflow Gen2 partitions data by a datetime column and reprocesses only the configured recent window, leaving historical partitions untouched — the standard fix for full-reload pain. Disabling staging changes execution internals, duplicate dataflows double the waste, and fast copy accelerates ingestion but doesn't skip unchanged history.
